{{nihongo|'''Makata Shrine'''|麻賀多神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shimōsa Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} system it was a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. It is the head shrine of the "18 Makata Shrines" (Makata Juhassha) in the {{ill|Inba District area|ja|印旛郡市|qid=Q11409099}}.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, in the 42nd year of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}} (AD 113), {{ill|Yamato Takeru|arz|ياماتو تاكيرو|be|Ямата Такэру|de|Yamatotakeru|es|Yamato Takeru|fa|یاماتو تاکه‌رو|fr|Yamato Takeru|hu|Jamatotakeru|id|Yamato Takeru|it|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|ko|야마토타케루|pt|Yamato Takeru|ru|Ямато Такэру|sh|Yamato Takeru|simple|Yamato Takeru|sq|Jamato Takeru|sr|Јамато Такеру|sv|Yamato Takeru|tr|Yamato Takeru|uk|Ямато Такеру|ur|یاماتو تاکیرو|vi|Yamato Takeru|zh|日本武尊|zh_min_nan|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto}} visited this area while on his eastern campaign, hung a mirror on a cedar trunk, and said: "If you revere and worship this mirror as Inba-no-Kunitama-Okitsukagami, the five grains will be abundant." This is said to be the origin of the shrine. In the 20th year of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}, Itokori-no-Mikoto, the 8th-generation descendant of {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|fr|Kamuyaimimi|ja|神八井耳命|ko|카무야이미미노미코토|simple|Kamuyaimimi|zh|神八井耳命|qid=Q11588756}} and the {{ill|Inba no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|印波国造|qid=Q11409105|lt=Inba no Kuni no Miyatsuko}}, built a shrine hall at present-day Funagata in Narita and enshrined Wakahirume-no-Mikoto with that mirror as the {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}}. Itokori-no-Mikoto also dug up seven jewels from beneath the cedar and additionally enshrined Wakumusubi-no-Kami with them as shintai. These two deities were called the "great deities of Makata no Ma" (magatama). In the 16th year of {{ill|Empress Suiko|Q298057|qid=Q298057}} (AD 608), Hirokushi Tekurohiko-no-Mikoto, the 8th-generation descendant of Itokori-no-Mikoto, transferred Wakumusubi-no-Kami to present-day Daikata in Narita by divine oracle, and the former shrine became the Okumiya.

When it was recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, because "Makata no Ma" shared a name with one of the {{ill|Imperial Regalia of Japan|Q327465|qid=Q327465}}, one character was taken and the name was changed to "Makata Shrine." Later, because the area was a hemp-producing region, the shrine name was changed to "Asakata (Makata) Shrine."

=== Okumiya ===
Located in Teguros, Funagata, Narita, and called Teguro-sha. It is the inner shrine of Daikata.

=== Other Makata Shrines ===
Shrines named "Makata Shrine" number 18 in the {{ill|Inba District|Q677245|qid=Q677245|lt=Inba area}}: one in Narita including Daikata, eleven in {{ill|Sakura, Chiba|Q498011|qid=Q498011}}, two in {{ill|Shisui|Q782157|qid=Q782157}}, two in {{ill|Tomisato|Q692857|qid=Q692857}}, and one in {{ill|Yachiyo, Chiba|Q328651|qid=Q328651}}. It is a rare shrine name nationwide, and these shrines exist only from the east side of {{ill|Inbanuma|Q5120731|qid=Q5120731}} southward.

* {{ill|Makata Shrine|Q11677653|qid=Q11677653}}
* {{ill|Makata- Shrine|Q24876715|qid=Q24876715}}

=== Cultural properties ===
[[ファイル:Makatajinjya-koudunooosugi.jpg|thumb|200px|The great {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=cedar}} at Makata Shrine, also called "Kozu no Ōsugi."]] 

The following are designated {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|fa|املاک فرهنگی (ژاپن)|fr|Patrimoine culturel du Japon|id|Properti Kebudayaan (Jepang)|ja|文化財|tr|Kültürel Varlık (Japonya)|zh|日本文化财|qid=Q858308}}<ref name="CityBunkazai">{{Cite web|和書|author=Narita City Board of Education Lifelong Learning Division|url=https://www.city.narita.chiba.jp/bunka_sports/page215300.html|title=Notice and use of cultural properties (list of cultural properties)|work=Narita City, Chiba Prefecture|accessdate=2021-04-24}}</ref>.

* Prefecturally designated {{ill|Natural monument|Q23790|qid=Q23790}}
** Forest of Makata Shrine - designated {{ill|March 8|Q2395|qid=Q2395}} {{ill|1977|Q2481|qid=Q2481}} (Showa 52). The designated area is 6,386 square meters of shrine grove land{{R|"CityBunkazai"}}. In addition to more than 20 {{ill|Cryptomeria|Q147388|qid=Q147388}} trees, species such as {{ill|Cyclobalanopsis|Q796117|qid=Q796117}} and {{ill|Castanopsis|Q1065400|qid=Q1065400}} grow there. The "Kozu no Ōsugi," traditionally said to be 1,200-1,300 years old, is especially a giant tree about 40 meters tall with a trunk circumference of about 8 meters<ref name="moriChibaPref">{{Cite web |和書 |url=https://www.pref.chiba.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/bunkazai/p431-063.html |title=Forest of Makata Shrine / Chiba Prefecture |website=Official Chiba Prefecture Website (www.pref.chiba.lg.jp) |publisher=Chiba Prefectural Government |date=2024-02-27 |access-date=2025-04-21}}</ref>.
* City-designated {{ill|Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|Q2901860|qid=Q2901860}}
** Main hall of Makata Shrine - designated {{ill|November 3|Q2995|qid=Q2995}} {{ill|1971|Q2475|qid=Q2475}} (Showa 46).
* City-designated {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Intangible Folk Cultural Property}} 
** Makata Shrine Kagura - designated {{ill|October 6|Q2928|qid=Q2928}} {{ill|1975|Q2479|qid=Q2479}} (Showa 50).
* City-designated {{ill|Historic site|Q1081138|qid=Q1081138}}
** Shikinaisha Makata Shrine - designated November 3, {{ill|1969|Q2485|qid=Q2485}} (Showa 44).
